_readme: Error lines (T37): what the player reads when an AI call fails. Each line says what went wrong in its first sentence, then makes a joke in the show's playful, petty voice. The first line of each case is the one approved on 2026-11-15; the second is in the same voice. The game picks one of a case's lines at random.

Read by BPC_LLMClient.ErrorLine(Kind, Lab, N, Type). Every place that writes error text uses it: OnHealth, the two GoDown calls in HandleHttp, OnKeyTest, KeyTestResult and SetMode, and the backstage note when an actor's reply fails after its retry.

Case keys. A plain key is a kind that BPC_LLMClient.ErrorKind returns, so the game can use it as it is. A key that starts with a screen name (health_, down_, keytest_) is that screen's own line for a kind: the caller tries '<screen>_<kind>' first, then '<kind>'. The screens match the 'where' in the log line NHOS: ERROR <kind> provider=<id> where=<health|down|keytest|turn>.

The unavailable screen, before a relay show (OnHealth, where=health): health_no_reply (the relay doesn't answer), health_unreadable (its reply can't be read), health_too_few_labs (fewer than 3 labs can serve calls), and the relay's own error types budget_used_up, session_limit, player_limit and provider_unavailable.

The unavailable screen, during a relay show (GoDown in HandleHttp, where=down): down_no_reply (the relay stopped answering), or the relay's type (budget_used_up, session_limit, player_limit, provider_unavailable). For a relay type with no case here, the relay's own error.message stays the fallback.

Backstage notes during a show (where=turn), one per kind: out_of_credits, rate_limited, overloaded, key_rejected, no_reply, cut_off, refused, unreadable, relay_429 (the lab said 429 through the relay, which can't tell a rate limit from our spending cap), relay_provider (any other relay provider_error) and unknown.

The key screen (OnKeyTest, KeyTestResult and SetMode, where=keytest): keytest_no_keys (Test keys with nothing pasted), keytest_too_few_keys (Save and Play with keys for fewer than 3 labs), keytest_key_rejected, keytest_out_of_credits and keytest_no_reply (one lab's test result), keytest_all_pass (every pasted key works). A key-test failure of any other kind falls back to its plain kind.

Placeholders, and only these: {lab} = the provider's display name, its 'name' in personas.json (OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI or Meta). {n} = a count: how many labs the relay can reach (health_too_few_labs) or how many keys passed (keytest_all_pass). {type} = the error's 'type' field as the provider or the relay sent it, such as authentication_error. Both lines of a case use the same placeholders.

Never put the provider's own error message in a line: some providers echo part of the key (T21). ErrorKind reads it only for keywords. No persona names (the bots go by their provider, and that comes from {lab}), no lab name written out, no real people's names.
Tools/check_prompts.py --offline checks this file: every case has its lines, no unknown case or placeholder, and no persona name, lab name or banned name.

health_no_reply: The AI relay isn't answering: it's down, or you're offline. The robots are standing in the dark, waiting for their cue.
The game can't reach the AI relay: it's down, or your internet is. The cast is in the green room, refusing to come out.
health_unreadable: The AI relay answered, but the game can't read the reply. Even the robots couldn't make sense of it.
The AI relay sent back a reply the game doesn't understand. Somebody handed out the wrong script.
budget_used_up: Today's free AI budget is used up (it resets at midnight UTC). Our producers are cheap and burned it all.
Today's free AI budget has run out (it resets at midnight UTC). The producers spent it all on craft services.
health_too_few_labs: The relay can reach only {n} of the 4 AI labs, and a show needs 3. Half the cast called in sick.
Only {n} of the 4 AI labs are answering the relay, and a show needs 3. The rest of the cast is stuck in traffic.
session_limit: This show has used all its free AI calls. The producers cut the budget mid-scene. Enter your own API keys to finish.
This show is out of free AI calls. The money ran out before the final act. Enter your own API keys to see how it ends.
player_limit: You've used all of today's free AI calls. That's a lot of improv. Enter your own keys, or come back tomorrow.
Your free AI calls for today are all used up. You've earned a standing ovation, and a break. Enter your own keys, or come back tomorrow.
provider_unavailable: The relay has no key for {lab}, so {lab} can't go on. Someone forgot to sign its contract.
The relay isn't set up with a key for {lab}, so {lab} can't perform. Its agent never returned our calls.
down_no_reply: The AI relay stopped answering: it went down, or your connection dropped. The lights are on, but nobody's home.
The game lost the AI relay mid-show: it went down, or your connection did. Someone tripped over the power cable backstage.
out_of_credits: {lab}'s API key is out of credits, so it has no tokens left to think with. Whoever owns that key is cheap. (If it's yours: hi.)
{lab}'s API key has run out of credits, so it can't afford another word. Somebody's been skipping the bills.
rate_limited: {lab} hit its rate limit: too many requests, too fast. It's on a mandatory union break.
{lab} is rate limited: it got too many requests in too short a time. It's been sent to its trailer to cool off.
overloaded: {lab}'s servers are full right now, so its line never came. Everyone else is asking {lab} for things too.
{lab} is overloaded right now and couldn't take this request. It's doing a matinee for the rest of the internet.
key_rejected: {lab} rejected its API key (wrong, expired or revoked). It won't perform without a valid contract.
{lab} didn't accept its API key (it's wrong, expired or revoked). Security won't let it past the stage door.
no_reply: {lab} never answered: the request timed out or the connection dropped. It froze like it forgot its lines.
{lab}'s reply never arrived: the request timed out or the connection broke. It's standing in the wings, staring into space.
cut_off: {lab}'s reply hit its length limit and got cut mid-sentence. It was going to be brilliant. Probably.
{lab}'s reply ran past its length limit and was cut off before the end. The director yelled 'cut' a little too early.
refused: {lab}'s safety filter refused this line. Very principled. Very method.
{lab} refused to give this line because its safety filter stepped in. It has notes on the script.
unreadable: {lab} answered, but in a shape the game can't read. It ad-libbed so hard it broke the script.
{lab} replied in a format the game can't read. It's speaking in interpretive dance.
relay_429: {lab} told the relay 'too many requests': it's rate limited, or our producers hit their spending cap.
The relay got 'too many requests' back from {lab}: it's rate limited, or we hit our spending cap. Either way, {lab} is taking five.
relay_provider: {lab} didn't answer through the relay; the problem is on {lab}'s end. It'll try again next turn.
The relay reached {lab}, but {lab} had a problem on its end. It's backstage fixing a costume malfunction and will try again next turn.
unknown: {lab}'s request failed with an error the game doesn't recognize ({type}). It's improvising silence.
{lab} failed with an error the game has never seen before ({type}). Call it a dramatic pause.
keytest_no_keys: Paste at least one key to test. The robots don't work for exposure.
No keys are pasted in yet, so there's nothing to test. No key, no audition.
keytest_too_few_keys: Enter keys for at least 3 of the 4 AI labs. A show needs a cast, not a monologue.
Add keys for at least 3 of the 4 AI labs to start a show. Anything less is a podcast.
keytest_key_rejected: {lab}: key rejected ({type}). It's not you, it's the key.
{lab}: the key didn't work ({type}). The bouncer says it's not on the list.
keytest_out_of_credits: {lab}: out of credits. Someone's been cheap.
{lab}: the key works, but it has no credits left. Time to pass the hat.
keytest_all_pass: All {n} keys work. The cast is hired.
All {n} keys passed the test. Places, everyone!
